title: Ghost Jobs: The Real Reason You’re Not Getting Interviews
description:
1 In 3 Jobs You Apply To Are Ghost Jobs


You applied to 30 jobs this month and 9 of them never existed. They were ghost listings: roles already filled, pipeline posts, compliance theatre, or harvests built to collect CVs. Around 30% of UK job postings right now aren't attached to a real, immediate hire. This video shows you the 5 signs a job is a ghost, the 3 channels where the real jobs actually live, and the 48-hour timing rule that decides whether your application even gets read.


What you'll learn in this video:
- What a ghost job actually is, and the 4 types companies post
- The 5 signs a listing is a ghost, so you can spot one in 30 seconds
- Why 30 of every 100 board applications were never going to get a reply
- The 3 channels where real jobs live, and the 30/30/40 time split that works
- The 48-hour rule that decides whether your application even gets read


VIDEO CHAPTERS:
0:00 9 of your 30 applications never existed
1:04 What a ghost job actually is (4 types)
2:35 Sign 1: posted for 30+ days
2:55 Sign 2: generic description
3:14 Sign 3: no named hiring manager
3:34 Sign 4: repeated reposts
3:51 Sign 5: lazy default application form
4:16 Where the real jobs actually live
5:54 The 30/30/40 allocation that works
6:15 The 48-hour rule
7:04 Audit your last 30 applications


Stop pouring applications into listings that were never real, and start spending that time where the offers actually come from. Here's how I can help:

The Offer Accelerator is my full system for landing offers faster. Personal brand, CV, LinkedIn, networking, applications, interviews, the lot.

Stop Applying Online | How to Land a Job in the Hidden Job Market


ABOUT ME:
I dropped out of university at 19 to build recruitment software and ATS systems used by hiring teams. For years I spoke to hundreds of hiring managers and recruiters every day, learning exactly how candidates get filtered, shortlisted, and hired from the inside. I started coaching friends through their job search using what I'd seen, then raised investment, built a software company, and hired my own team. I've seen hiring from every angle.

Today I help job seekers land offers faster using a proven 3-step system. I've coached hundreds of candidates into roles at firms like JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Deloitte, EY, and PwC and many more.


#jobsearch #careeradvice #ghostjobs

Are you applying to ghost jobs? Learn how to spot fake job postings and save hours on your job search with these practical identification methods.

Ghost jobs are listings that remain active on boards despite companies not actively hiring for the role. With research suggesting nearly 30% of postings fall into this category, understanding the signs of these inactive listings is essential for anyone currently looking for work. This guide breaks down five key indicators to help you avoid wasting time on applications that will never lead to an interview.

We examine common red flags, such as roles posted for over 30 days or positions that appear to be reposted repeatedly. By learning to identify ghost jobs early, you can refine your job search tips and focus your energy on active opportunities. Use these insights to improve your career strategy and filter out listings that are unlikely to result in a hire.

Subscribe for weekly career strategy breakdowns, and comment below if you have ever spotted a suspicious listing while hunting for work.
transcript: You are applying to ghost listings, they're sitting on LinkedIn and indeed, they're harvesting your data and they're roles that were probably filled 6 months ago. And the figure that keeps coming back is one in three. So, about 30% of job postings right now are not active hires. So, in the next few minutes, I'm going to walk you through what ghost jobs actually are and why companies post them. I'm going to show you the five signs that a listing is a ghost post and I'm going to show you how to spot one inside 30 seconds and then where the real jobs actually live, including the three channels that have dramatically higher conversion rates. All right, so let's get into it. So, the maths is brutal. So, the UK average for a role is 280 applications and 75% of the CVs get rejected by an ATS before a human sees them. And to top that all off, 30% of the postings you send out they're not even real. So, out of the 100 applications that you send on job boards, roughly 30 are just going into that void and there were never going to be interviews. The other 70 are going up against 280 applicants and they're being filtered out by software that's looking for specific wording. So, let me start with what a ghost post actually is because most candidates don't really know what they're looking at. So, a ghost job is a listing that isn't attached to a real immediate hiring decision. And there's four main types. So, the first type is that it's an old listing that never got taken down. The role was filled a few months ago, the recruiter or someone just forgot to deactivate the posting. And it sits there collecting hundreds of applications every week. From what I've tracked over the years, this is the most common category by a long way. The second type is the pipeline building post. So, companies that aren't actually hiring right now, but they want to keep CVs flowing in so then, you know, if they do hire, they've got a pool to pull from. So, the team exists, the roles are plausible, but the application just isn't really ready to be interviewed because nobody's actively reading that inbox. The third type is then the compliance post. So, internal hires get made all the time, but some companies are required by policy to also post a role externally. So, the role is filled, the internal candidate is already chosen, but the external listing is just there for compliance. And then the fourth type is then the harvest. So, smaller companies, recruitment agencies, and some other platforms, they post fake jobs purely to collect data. They build their database to test the market without any real hiring intent. So, when you apply to 100 jobs on LinkedIn and you hear back from three, the problem often isn't really your CV. About 30 of those 100 jobs were just ghost listings before you even hit send. They were never going to reply to anyone. So, now let me walk you through the five signs that a listing is probably a ghost post. So, sign one is that the job has been posted for more than 30 days. Most legitimate UK roles should fill within 21 days. If a listing has been sitting there for 6-8 weeks, then there's a high chance the company has either already hired or just stopped actively reviewing. So, check the posted date before you apply. Now, the second sign is the description that is generic and could apply to half a dozen different companies. Ghost listings often recycle template language because nobody actually wrote them for a specific role. Real listings tend to describe the team, the tools, and the actual projects, even things like the manager style. Ghost posts read like a job spec generator that was AI-generated. Now, for sign three, um this is basically where no named hiring manager or recruiter is attached. So, legitimate roles usually have somebody behind them. Now, they're either named in the listing, they're named on LinkedIn job page, or they're findable in a 60-second search of the company's people directory. If you can't find anybody who would actually be receiving the application, that's a bit of a red flag. Now, sign four is that the company has reposted the same role multiple times in the last 12 months. So, some roles are genuinely hard to fill, but if you see the same job description from the same company posted in March and then in June and then October, then the listing isn't really real hiring activity. It's a pipeline post. Now, the fifth sign is the application form is lazy automatic one with no tailored questions. So, real hiring manager often ask two or three role-specific questions in the application form. Now, ghost listings, they typically rely on default ATS form because nobody's actually reading the answers. So, if a listing trips two or more of those signs, you can skip it. And if it's three or more, then definitely skip it. So, that should get you out of the trap. Now, let me tell you where the real jobs actually live because most candidates, they only check on public job boards. And that's where the ghost posts are the densest. So, most of you, you're spending about 95% of your time on the job search on LinkedIn, Indeed, Google Jobs, things like that. And the candidates who actually get hired in this market spread their effort across three different channels. So, channel one is the public job board. That's obviously LinkedIn, Indeed, Google Jobs, Glassdoor. It's high volume, easy to access, but also where most of the ghost listings sit. Conversion rates from public boards are typically 1 to 3%. So, use them for volume, but shouldn't be for a primary conversion. Now, the second channel is direct on company website pages. The company's own website, applying through their career section, that's where you need to be. Now, there's slightly fewer applications because some candidates just can't be bothered. And you can often see the full organizations, like other open roles as well. Now, conversion rates are usually 3 to 5% on here. And then channel three is the hidden job market. So, this is referrals, networking-driven applications, and direct outreach. Referred candidates convert at 15 to 30%. Networked applications with a name drop convert at 10 to 20%. So, these conversion rates would be massively higher than the public boards because the trust layer is already in place. The hiring manager isn't filtering blindly. They're considering somebody who's been pre-vetted by someone they trust. So, the rough allocation that actually works is about 30% of your application time on public job boards, 30% on direct career pages, and those like niche job boards, and then 40% on the hidden job market. Now, most candidates have this completely wrong. They're spending 95% of their time in the channel with the lowest conversion rates and the highest ghost job density. So, one more thing before I wrap up because this one alone changes the math on every application you send. When a real role gets posted, most of the strong applications come in the first 48 hours. And by hour 40, the recruiter often has about 50 to 100 applications. And by the end of week one, 2 to 500. So, roles often start interviewing once they have about five strong candidates. If those five came from the first 48 hours, the role is effectively closed before the rest of the applications are even reviewed. So, if you're applying 4 days after a role posts, you're competing with a pipeline that's already made the process. So, the rule is simple. Apply within the first 48 hours of a role being posted whenever possible. Set daily alerts on LinkedIn, Indeed, and the niche job boards so you find the roles inside hours, not days. And if you missed the first 48 hours, there's a smaller second window. It's about 10 to 14 days. So, if you take one thing from this video, just audit your last 30 applications. Look at how many of those listings, you know, have been up for more than 4 weeks. Or they had no named hiring manager. Or they used template generic language. Or they showed up as repeated reposts. A massive chunk of them are probably ghost jobs. And those applications were never going to come back. So, no matter how good your CV looked. Now, I spent the last 5 years building recruitment software and ATS systems. And I've put together a massive list of niche job boards and seven job search methodologies that are outside the conventional strategies. So, if you want access to that today, the link is in the description for the Offer Accelerator. And that will teach you step-by-step exactly how to convert interviews into your target offers.
